metadata.title: Unit Circle and Sine Height
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Connect a point on the unit circle to the height of the sine curve.
metadata.learner: Knows right-triangle ratios; has not connected circular motion to sine.
misconceptions: Sine is only a triangle ratio
The sine value is the x-coordinate
expectedUnderstanding: The y-coordinate of the unit-circle point is sin(theta)
The sine curve records the same height as the angle turns
Height is zero at 0 and 180 degrees and maximal at 90 degrees

checkpoints.title: Height at 0 degrees
checkpoints.body: Set the angle to 0 degrees. The point sits on the positive x-axis, so its y-coordinate and sine are 0.

checkpoints.title: Height at 90 degrees
checkpoints.body: Set the angle to 90 degrees. The point is at the top of the circle; its y-coordinate and sine are 1.

checkpoints.title: Height at 180 degrees
checkpoints.body: Set the angle to 180 degrees. The point is on the negative x-axis; its height and sine are 0 again.

narration.text: Drag the angle slider. Watch the horizontal guide tie the circle's height to the sine curve.
At 90 degrees the point is at the top of the circle; its height is 1.
At 180 degrees the point returns to the axis; the sine height is 0.

fallback.text: A point on the unit circle has height sin(theta). At 0 and 180 degrees the height is 0; at 90 degrees it is 1. The sine curve at right plots that same height as the angle increases.

accessibility.alt: Unit circle at left with a radius to a movable angle point, a horizontal guide to a sine curve at right, and matching vertical height lines. A slider changes the angle from 0 to 360 degrees.
